paras.en: On the fifth day, again thanks to the sheep, this secret of the little prince’s life was revealed to me. He asked me abruptly, without a word of introduction, as though his question had grown out of a problem he had long thought over in silence:
paras.zh: 第五天，还是多亏了那只羊，我才知道小王子生活中的这个秘密。他突然问我，一句开场白也没有，仿佛这个问题是他默默思索了很久才结出的果实：

paras.en: “If a sheep eats shrubs, does it eat flowers too?”
paras.zh: “羊要是吃灌木，那也吃花吗？”

paras.en: “A sheep eats everything it comes across.”
paras.zh: “羊碰到什么就吃什么。”

paras.en: “Even flowers with thorns?”
paras.zh: “连长着刺的花也吃吗？”

paras.en: “Yes. Even flowers with thorns.”
paras.zh: “是的。连长着刺的花也吃。”

paras.en: “Then what are thorns for?”
paras.zh: “那刺有什么用呢？”

paras.en: I did not know. Just then I was very busy trying to unscrew a bolt on my engine that was too tight. I was very worried: the breakdown was beginning to seem very serious, and my dwindling drinking water made me fear the worst.
paras.zh: 我不知道。当时我正忙着想拧下发动机上一颗拧得太紧的螺栓。我很发愁，因为我开始觉得这次故障非常严重，而饮用水也快耗尽了，让我担心最坏的事情会发生。

paras.en: “What are thorns for?”
paras.zh: “刺有什么用呢？”

paras.en: The little prince never let go of a question once he had asked it. I was annoyed with my bolt and said the first thing that came into my head:
paras.zh: 小王子一旦提出一个问题，就从来不肯放下。我被那颗螺栓弄得心烦，便随口胡说了一句：

paras.en: “Thorns are no use at all. The flowers do it out of pure spite!”
paras.zh: “刺一点用也没有，纯粹是花在使坏！”

paras.en: “Oh!”
But after a silence he shot back, with a kind of resentment:
paras.zh: 可是，沉默了一会儿，他带着几分怨气，向我甩来一句话：

paras.en: “I don’t believe you! Flowers are weak. They are naïve. They reassure themselves as best they can. They think they are fearsome with their thorns...”
paras.zh: “我不信你的话！花儿很弱小。她们很天真。她们尽自己所能让自己安心。她们以为有了刺，自己就很吓人了……”

paras.en: I said nothing. At that moment I was thinking: “If this bolt still won’t budge, I’ll knock it off with one blow of my hammer.” The little prince interrupted my thoughts again:
paras.zh: 我什么也没回答。那一刻，我心里正想着：“要是这颗螺栓还不松动，我就一锤子把它敲掉。”小王子又打断了我的思绪：

paras.en: “And you, do you believe that flowers...”
paras.zh: “那你呢，你觉得花儿……”

paras.en: “No! No! I don’t believe anything! I just said whatever came into my head. I’m busy with serious things!”
paras.zh: “不是！不是！我没什么看法！我只是随口乱说的。我正忙着做正经事呢！”

paras.en: He looked at me, astonished.
paras.zh: 他望着我，惊呆了。

paras.en: “Serious things!”
paras.zh: “正经事！”

paras.en: He saw me, hammer in hand and fingers black with grease, bent over an object that looked very ugly to him.
paras.zh: 他看见我手里握着锤子，手指被油垢染得黑黑的，俯身对着一个在他看来很丑的东西。

paras.en: “You talk like grown-ups!”
paras.zh: “你说话跟大人们一样！”

paras.en: That made me feel a little ashamed. But he showed no mercy and added:
paras.zh: 这让我有点惭愧。可他毫不留情，又加了一句：

paras.en: “You confuse everything... you mix everything up!”
paras.zh: “你什么都分不清……你把什么都混在一起！”

paras.en: He really was very angry. He shook his golden hair in the wind:
paras.zh: 他真的气坏了。他在风中甩着一头金灿灿的头发：

paras.en: “I know a planet where there is a crimson gentleman. He has never smelt a flower. He has never looked at a star. He has never loved anyone. He has never done anything but add up numbers. And all day long he repeats, just like you: ‘I am a serious man! I am a serious man!’ And that makes him swell with pride. But he is not a man, he is a mushroom!”
paras.zh: “我知道一个星球，上面有位红得发紫的先生。他从没闻过一朵花。他从没看过一颗星星。他从没爱过任何人。他除了做加法，从没做过别的事。他还整天像你一样反复说：‘我是个正经人！我是个正经人！’这让他骄傲得膨胀起来。可他不是人，他是个蘑菇！”

paras.en: “A what?”
paras.zh: “是个什么？”

paras.en: “A mushroom!”
paras.zh: “是个蘑菇！”

paras.en: The little prince was now quite pale with anger.
paras.zh: 小王子这时已经气得脸色煞白。

paras.en: “For millions of years, flowers have been making thorns. For millions of years, sheep have been eating flowers all the same. And isn't it serious to try to understand why they go to so much trouble to make themselves thorns that are never any use at all? Isn't the war between sheep and flowers important? Isn't it more serious and more important than a fat red gentleman's sums? And if I myself know a flower that is the only one of its kind in the world, that exists nowhere except on my planet, and that a little sheep can destroy in one go, just like that, one morning, without realising what it is doing—that isn't important!”
paras.zh: “花儿给自己长出刺，已经有几百万年了。羊照样吃花，也已经有几百万年了。想弄明白花儿为什么那么费劲，给自己长出从来都毫无用处的刺，这难道不是正经事？羊和花儿之间的战争，难道不重要？难道不比一个红脸胖先生做加法更正经、更重要？而如果我，我认识一朵世上独一无二的花，除了我的星球，别处哪里都没有，而一只小羊，在某个早晨，就能那么一下子把她彻底毁掉，连自己在做什么都不知道，这难道还不重要！”

paras.en: He flushed, then went on:
paras.zh: 他的脸涨红了，又接着说：

paras.en: “If someone loves a flower that is the only one of its kind among millions and millions of stars, that is enough to make him happy when he looks at them. He says to himself: ‘My flower is out there somewhere...’ But if the sheep eats the flower, it is as though all the stars suddenly went out for him! And that isn't important!”
paras.zh: “如果有人爱着一朵花，在几百万又几百万颗星星中只有这么一朵，那么，他看着那些星星时，就足够感到幸福了。他会对自己说：‘我的花就在那里的某个地方……’可要是羊吃掉了那朵花，对他来说，就好像所有星星突然全都熄灭了！这难道还不重要！”

paras.en: He could say no more. He suddenly burst into sobs. Night had fallen. I had dropped my tools. I did not care at all about my hammer, my bolt, thirst or death. On a star, a planet, my own, the Earth, there was a little prince to comfort! I took him in my arms. I rocked him. I was saying to him: “The flower you love is not in danger... I’ll draw a muzzle for him, for your sheep... I’ll draw you some armour for your flower... I...” I did not quite know what to say. I felt very clumsy. I did not know how to reach him, where to meet him... The land of tears is so mysterious!
paras.zh: 他再也说不出话来。他突然放声抽泣。夜已经降临。我已放下了工具。我的锤子、我的螺栓、口渴和死亡，我全都不在乎了。在一颗星星上，一颗行星上，我的行星——地球上，有一个小王子等着安慰！我把他抱在怀里。我轻轻摇着他。我对他说着：“你爱的那朵花没有危险……我会给它画一个嘴套，给你的绵羊……我会给你画一副给你的花穿的盔甲……我……”我不太知道该说些什么。我觉得自己十分笨拙。我不知道怎样才能走近他，到哪里才能与他相遇……多么神秘啊，这眼泪的国度！
